utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I apologise that we were delayed a little coming in. Good morning to you, Mr. Vilicic. If I could remind you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- the affirmation you took still applies. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. Vilicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Weiner: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, we have 30 minutes or maybe even less than 30 minutes to go. We could move very quickly if when I ask you questions, "are you aware," if you could just yes or no if you're aware of a certain subject. I'll be asking you for your opinion at certain times, and then you can expand and offer your opinion and explanations. That's fine. If you can just please try and answer the questions in as short an answer as possible, we can get this done very quickly. Yesterday, we left discussing the vehicle named Charlie. And the statement of Slobodan Simonovic that you cited in your report. Do you recall that? We left discussing those subjects or we ended the day discussing those subjects.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know, sir, that in the Simonovic statement, the Slobodan Simonovic statement, he does not ever state that Charlie was located just north of the Old Town walls. You know that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he didn't mention that. Only I don't know which location you are referring particularly. If you are talking about C-6, I said that that was the target that we had taken as a mobile weapon, which is at the location 500 metres from the walls. And we discussed whether in that particular case the shells fell inside the city walls. We named it Charlie, but in fact that was C-6 because nowhere in any report there was any mention of any weapon at that particular location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "at that particular location," you're indicating there was no mention of any weapon north of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: North of the Old Town was a vehicle, that is 100 metres north to the Old Town. And I heard that throughout the testimonies here. I dubbed it Charlie, this location. But it involves C-5 and C-6 because that was at 100 metres before that we had C-4 and C-3 at 200 and 300 metres. And as I said recently, we assumed C-6 at 500 metres in order to estimate whether this particular location would jeopardise the Old Town or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Simonovic, Slobodan Simonovic, never states that he saw Charlie north of the Old Town. He never states that in his statement. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you know, Mr. Simonovic didn't live in the Old Town, he lived well west of the Old Town. And that's where he saw Charlie. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I never established a link between Simonovic and Charlie. I mentioned Simonovic for the reason of his saying that the vehicle had come to their street and shot from there, and then went back again. It was a vehicle-mounted weapon, and that is the type when those four or five buildings were demolished.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you also know that Mr. Simonovic never saw Charlie in the area of the Old Town on the 6th of December 1991 because he was back at his home or in a shelter near his home far away from the Old Town. Mr. Simonovic never indicates in his report that you cited that he saw Charlie on December 6th. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I'm saying again that I never connected Simonovic and the location 100 metres north of the town or the C-6 location. There is no relation whatsoever between that and Simonovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that three Defence witnesses who claimed to have seen Charlie have placed it in Lapad and do not mention seeing it north of the Old Town in December 1991? Those are witnesses Novakovic, Lemal, and Pavisic. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not because I was very busy by complying with your request to provide an English version of the annex, and I really have no information whatsoever about any testimonies given in the past two weeks. Therefore, I didn't have an opportunity to listen to either Lemal, Novakovic, and I don't know which was the third person that you mentioned. Primic or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pavisic.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pavisic, no I had no opportunity to hear that testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you're further aware -- having monitored the case, you're aware Mr. Negodic places Charlie in Lapad in December, one vehicle named Charlie in Lapad? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard Negodic's testimony, and I did that very carefully. I'm not sure whether I managed to hear every single word because connections, especially audio connections sometimes fail. But I did hear his whole testimony because it was particularly interesting for this expert analysis, and that is why I invoked his testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that the only person who claims to have seen a single vehicle named Charlie, not multiple vehicles as you mentioned in your report, but a single vehicle named Charlie was the witness who preceded you, who claimed to have seen it north of the Old Town on December 6th, Mr. Nesic? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware. I was here in The Hague when he testified, but I had no chance to listen to his testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you concluded that fire from the Charlie vehicles located - and this is on page 99 - that fire from the Charlie vehicles located north and west of the Old Town increased the number of shells falling into the Old Town. Didn't you make that conclusion in your report, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I keep saying that we should speak in conditional. If Charlie vehicles were operative, or rather the weapons were operating from vehicles to the west or north of the town, that contributed to an increased number of the shells falling. Practically, the whole report, the paper was prepared in order to serve the Trial Chamber when they consider various statements made, the majority of which I had heard except for the last one that you mentioned, that there is a possibility to judge from a professional point of view what would happen if some conditions were met. That is how I perceived this analysis, that its terms of reference were to provide a basis to judge the testimony of various witnesses. If a witness said that Charlie was at a certain location, to decide whether it posed a danger to the Old Town. That is why we took C-6 and assumed that if Charlie was not officially defined as such, so if it was positioned or any other weapon was positioned, at least at 500 metres from the Old Town would not jeopardise the Old Town. So this is the purpose of this expert analysis. And that was our intention while we were preparing it. Our intention was not to say yes, there was a Charlie, or no there wasn't a Charlie. We worked on the assumptions if fire from VP-1 was opened at C-4, C-5, this and that would happen under certain conditions. So please understand that I am speaking conditionally, and you are talking in the present tense all the time. And you claim that Charlie was there. I never claimed that. I just made an assumption that had Charlie been there, this and that could have happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, the reason I asked you that question is because on page 88, your conclusion number 6, is not in a -- written in a conditional manner. What you write is: "What particularly contributed to a considerably higher number of projectiles landing in the Dubrovnik Old Town was firing from DOS artillery pieces mounted on Charlie mobile vehicles, which fired from the northern and western sides of the walls of Dubrovnik Old Town." Now, let's use your conditional "if." Since there is conflicting evidence as to Charlie, if we assume that Charlie was not present, that conclusion's no longer valid. We would have to find some other reasons for those shells landing in the Old Town, for those considerable higher number of projectiles landing in the Old Town. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, the Trial Chamber will hopefully, if it concludes that there was no weapon at this location, of course I will rule out this kind of conclusion. However, if there was a weapon at that location, and given the weather conditions and the proximity, what we wrote would have happened. So my conclusion was made on the basis that if Charlie was operating there, the other things were operating on the other location, weather conditions were there as they were, this would only contribute to an increased number of shells falling into the Old Town. So please, perceive this in that manner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. But look at my assumption. If Charlie was not there, we would have to find another reason for that increased number of shells landing in the Old Town. Isn't that correct? If we assume that Charlie or what you say multiple Charlies were not present on that day, we would have to find some other reason for multiple shells landing in the Old Town. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That will be up to the Trial Chamber hopefully to establish. It's not our business. But specifically, there were only two Charlie positions. An aircraft gun was at 100 metres north of town. Maybe I made a mistake. Instead of saying Charlie, I should have said anti-aircraft gun, and C-6 was a kind of conditional firing position that I studied only from the aspect whether it posed a danger to the town from that particular location. And I said that a firing position at 500 metres from the Old Town did not pose a risk to the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to two other locations, sir. You indicated that shells from JNA mortars fired at Bogosica Park and Ploce also landed in the Old Town. And you based those locations on the statements of Nojko Marinovic and Mr. Negodic. At trial, sir, Ivan Negodic testified that those positions were not active on December 6th, as you know listening to the case. Now, again, let's assume that there was no Croatian presence or no Croatian firing from Bogosica Park and Ploce on December 6. Your conclusion that those locations were primary targets would no longer be valid. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one cannot make this kind of conclusion. When the Croatian forces intensified their fire and if firing positions had not been located that had earlier been active, it is only logical that your primary target would be the positions that had been active up until then. The C-4 position marked by Mr. Negodic on the map 03340719 in annex number 4 clearly indicates that given the objectives of that firing position, the focus of the attack came precisely from that location that it should have covered in defence. If you look at Zarkovica, Zarkovica covers practically everything. Brgat, Bosanka, and one of the main direction of attacks of infantry JNA units on that day, according to all indications, was focussed on this particular position. So it is incomprehensible that out of the total of six or seven Croatian mortars, four of them were out of action under such circumstances. So if Negodic's statement is truthful, then your conclusion is valid. I hope that we are -- want to establish the truth and what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. Now, sir, are you aware that two Defence witnesses have alleged that JNA mortar fire was directed against alleged targets in the Old Town, and that's Mr. Vlado Pepic and Jovan Drljan. If objects or areas within the Old Town were targeted, wouldn't that change your estimate as to the number of shells falling in the Old Town? These two people have testified.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I hear of that, and I'm simply surprised at that. Those must have been laymen statements. If mortars are used to target objectives inside the town where you have very narrow streets, it is beyond comprehension, this is totally illogical, both militarily and otherwise, to shoot at roofs in order to hit someone on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Vlado Pepic was the observer for the 130-millimetre weapons. He was on Zarkovica looking down. Jovan Drljan, and I'll spell the last name, D-r-l-j-a-n, was a soldier. And these were two JNA soldiers. And they indicated there were flashes seen in the Old Town, or one did, and they fired mortars, Maljutkas, cannons or artillery, fired at those objects in the area of the Old Town and struck buildings. And my question to you is wouldn't that increase the numbers of shells that landed in the Old Town if they fired at things they thought were there?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, how it is possible for one soldier to fire from different weapons systems. This Drljan person, if he was operating a mortar, he could only have shot from a mortar. If he was handling a rocket launcher, then he could have only fired a rocket. And there were no artillery pieces active on that day, that had been established definitively, that not a single artillery projectile had fallen on the Old Town, and there was no artillery activity. On the contrary, it was established that there was a prohibition on artillery fire. If you want my expert opinion independently of what they stated, Maljutka can only shoot at the walls of the Old Town, nothing else. There is no chance for a single operator to throw a rocket inside the Old Town. I know the guidance system very well. You cannot guide that rocket and then just drop it there. It has to be a vertical target relative to the rocket launcher. That rocket does not have a so-called curved trajectory. It is introduced by straight-line trajectories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, once again, JNA witnesses have indicated that - I probably used the wrong word with artillery - cannon fire, Maljutka fire, and mortar fire was directed at the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. This is not in evidence. Cannon fire has not been established, nor has that been heard in this courtroom, and my learned friend will certainly remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the question is what description is given to the weapon at Zarkovica, if I'm right, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand it to be an artillery piece, not a Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am not entirely sure, but there is evidence of that having been used, I believe, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, it seems to me that my learned friend had mentioned JNA witnesses. He speaks of JNA witnesses who had seen cannon fire, Maljutka fire, and mortar fire. That was the essence of my objection. And you can see that, Your Honours, on line 9 -- on page 9, line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Once again, Mr. Petrovic, inevitably, all of us struggle in our precise memories of what occurred, and all of these matters have to be checked. Counsel have the advantage that they will have been looking at evidence on a particular point. But my impression is that if one leaves aside the Prosecution evidence and looks only at the Defence witnesses, there is evidence of three types of weapons being used from Zarkovica. But I may be wrong. That's just my present understanding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there is evidence from witnesses that served in the JNA on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let us take the Defence witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Defence witnesses, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On pages -- one is 7711 through 7713, which is Jovan Drljan, with a D, D-r-l-j-a-n. And Vlado Pepic at 7502 through 7503. That shells, mortar shells - between the two - they talk about mortar shells, Maljutkas were fired or landed in the Old Town as a result of what they thought to be targets. My question to you is if those shells --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let's not just blur over the point. From what you're saying, that doesn't extend to the third type of weapon at Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll read what Mr. Pepin [sic] said for the record, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Pepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Pepic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "And what targets were fired at from Zarkovica?" "As I started to say" - this is from page 7502 from Mr. Pepic; this is answer - "as I started to say, the firing came from targets, fire targets from a number of directions. Whether from Strincijera or the slopes of Srdj and the firing came, what I saw the firing came from the Maljutka laser weapon, the 9K-11. It was targeting the mortar, anti-cannon gun to the right and the mortar to the left and the mortar that I saw firing on the left-hand side on the street of the Stradun." And he had seen some flashes on the left-hand side, and he assumed it was a mortar. What Mr. Drljan says, on page 7711: "Q. Apart from that, did you see anything else in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a couple shells landing very close to the place where this mortar had been pulled out earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw mortars landing if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did it land?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Stradun street." And then they asked if you can please show the approximate position. "On the street itself. It's very close to the building from which the mortar had been pulled out and then been pulled in." And then Mr. Nesic testified that on the walls of the Old Town, there was a southern wall to the right of St. Blaise's church. I think it's St. Stjepan's tower, that they used a Maljutka or a recoilless weapon, and also on the walls they used Maljutka or recoilless weapons. My question to you is if objects were targeted within the Old Town, and you're familiar with that congested nature of the Old Town, wouldn't that increase the number of shells landing in the Old Town? Wouldn't that increase your conclusion as to the number of shells landing in the Old Town? Wouldn't you have to raise your estimate?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And here is why. If I understand you correctly, and if the interpretation was correct, all the weapons which you mentioned were on the Croatian side. The anti-armour company, I know this very well, had at Zarkovica in their weaponry six recoilless gun, two Maljutka rocket launchers, and I believe they had a 60-millimetre mortar. So they were able to shoot only from recoilless guns as we discussed yesterday, and with Maljutka rockets. Neither of these weapons are able to shoot at indirect targets. They cannot shoot at targets under cover. They can only shoot at targets in the direct line of sight. And they cause the kind of damage that was caused by mortar shells. First of all, these are not destructive projectiles; they are cumulative-charged projectile. They do not have the same destructive power. They don't have the high-impact power, and they could not shoot at targets within the Old Town. If they saw, for instance, something on the tower or on the walls or around the Old Town, they could have fired at that. But they could not have shot at a target within the walls of the Old Town, apart from targets that were in the direct line of sight from Zarkovica. And the only thing of that kind you could have seen would have been along the Stradun or in front of the walls or in front of the fish shop. Those are the targets that they could see. So these assumptions do not affect my expert opinion because we even stated clearly that we have no data for the hits on the walls or the towers. We only had data that mortar shells fell within the walls, damaging roofs or maybe the Stradun. I didn't encounter a single case where a projectile had managed to fall between the houses in one of those narrow streets. They damaged, for instance, ornaments at a higher level than ground level.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt this discussion. On page 12, look at the answer from line 12 onwards. It is not complete. There are certain parts of the answer missing, so I would appreciate it when we revise the transcript, especially the part where the witness said that from Zarkovica one could have shot at targets on the Stradun, if such had been detected. That part of the answer was not recorded, but we can easily check on the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Petrovic. Part of the problem is the speed and the length at which Mr. Vilicic speaks. The interpreters and the transcript cannot keep up. While we are paused, can I clear up a couple of matters that have me confused. Do I understand your evidence to be that the Maljutka is a line-of-sight weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you say it can't fire at targets in the Old Town, you mean it can only fire at targets that can be seen from the firing position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, sir. Guiding a rocket requires keeping a target in your sight constantly. The operator constantly keeps the crosshair on the target and keeps it higher than the target up to 100 to 200 metres before the target. And only when he reaches that distance from the target, he lowers it. In other words, he cannot shoot at a target behind the wall because it is a straight-line trajectory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That helps me to understand what you were saying. And the second matter is all the evidence tends to confirm what you indicated a moment ago. There was also a 60-millimetre mortar at Zarkovica. It could be fired in such a way as to target targets that were not in sight, but behind a weapon or below the line of sight. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but please, a 60-millimetre mortar has maximum range of 1700 metres. Or rather, it depends. We have two types of weapons. The JNA had two types of mortars. So in annex -- in one of the annexes to our expert opinion, we stated the performances of these weapons. And the first weapon in Annex 20 is a mortar that has initial speed -- in fact, its maximum range is 2.357 metres, whereas I know an old model had only 1.700 metres which was later increased. And now it has this maximum range of 2.357 metres with the fourth-last increment. So at the distance we discussed, that mortar could have fired at a target, let's say, 100 metres in front of the Old Town. But the shells could have not reached into the Old Town because if you look at where the Maljutkas were positioned, and I also have the exact location of recoilless guns, from that location to Old Town, the distance is 2.300-and-something metres. So they were somewhere next to the ancillary observation point of the battalion commander, and that location is over 2.300 metres. So at a stretch, a shell could have fallen somewhere between the ships. It could have fallen before the shore. It's -- the impact of this is like the combined effect of two hand grenades. That's the combined effect of this 60-millimetre shell. So they could not have had this destructive effect. They could have hit the roof, and maybe broken some tiles, but no important destruction.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, the part of the witness's answer that the counsel said was missing is on page 13, line 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, interpreters, for that. I take it the maximum range specification of a mortar is given on the assumption that both the firing position and the target are at the same elevation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This maximum range is true of table values. That means when the target and the firing position are at the same altitude, and the curvature of the trajectory is minimally -- minimally increases the range. They were at a height of 250 metres, which can increase the range by several dozen metres. I have this data here. Up to Kasa, it's 2.250 metres practically. So there was no chance that that mortar could have reached up to the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The mortar maximum range of 2.357 would be increased, according to the firing table graph at figure 2.25 in your annex 20. Is that right? According to the elevation of the firing point above the target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weiner, I'm sorry I interrupted. But two matters had left me unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, on the chart we can clearly see in this addendum that the range is increased very little. It is a negligible increase in range due to the difference in altitude.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, as these witnesses indicated that mortar shells --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there was evidence that fire was -- that mortar fire entered the Old Town targeting what was alleged to be a mortar. Wouldn't that increase the number of shells that would have landed in the Old Town, increase it above your estimates? Increase the number of shells?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is established that the Old Town was targeted intentionally, of course that would increase the number of projectiles. However, in our expert opinion, we contemplated shooting only at targets outside the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that, sir.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what we contemplated. It is logical that if the objective was to shoot at the Old Town, and I have a chart here, you would have a totally different picture of the projectiles landed and that picture in my expert opinion, 8.1, if you remember, it would look completely different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, if you were targeting a single mortar in the Old Town, that would not have caused all of that roof damage that we see in the Old Town. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I did not see all that damage because the damage described was not described in such a way as to say, for instance, the roof was damaged or the first floor was crashed through. We only reviewed damage in terms of the first, second, third degree with the exception of the first degree where the house is completely demolished, the following definitions were given. Several structures were damaged up to damage on the facade. The descriptions were not such as to lead me to conclude that there was a great number of roofs damaged. From the analysis that we made and objectively, knowing the efficiency, it was exactly established how much damage was done. It could have been 70 to 80 on the outside, not as it was initially written in one report, 450. But all this is conditionally speaking. My entire analysis is based on the "if this, then that." According to the rules of service, according to the norms, if a mortar was shooting at the Old Town foot destruction of such a target, according to norm number 17, at least 200 shells would have to have been fired. And that would have been a tragedy for the town. Look at annex 17. For the destruction of a firing position under cover or completely without any cover, it is necessary to fire 200 shells from a 120-millimetre mortar. The Old Town would have been destroyed. That is why I don't believe in such stories at all. Those mortars that were allegedly shot at by mortars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you agree that you do not fire at roofs; it's illogical as you just said to fire at roofs in an area. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to destroy a mortar that is on the ground, yes, it would clearly be illogical to target a mortar that cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So therefore, if all those roofs are damaged, and you saw numbers of roofs were damaged in the Old Town, there had to be some reason other than firing at one mortar. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, sir, above all, our expert opinion shows unequivocally that while shooting at targets that are around the town, some shells are bound to fall within the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the witness please be allowed to answer this question because he was stopped in midstream. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The problem, Mr. Petrovic, is that the answer is not dealing with the question. Normally, I would have agreed with you. But on this occasion, I think there was justification. So if you can get an answer to the question, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, based on the large number of roofs that had been damaged, all I'm saying is - just yes or no - there has to be some other reason than firing at one mortar. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Our expert analysis does not consider that at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, your expert analysis strictly dealt with firing at alleged targets outside of the Old Town. If shells were intentionally fired at objects within the Old Town, you would have to modify your conclusions, and you would have to modify your report. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the condition that I had reliable information about that to that effect, which we didn't, nor did our expert analysis require that. The expert analysis was written in order to ascertain whether during JNA fire against targets around the Old Town such as defined by Nojko Marinovic and others, those are the firing positions that I'm referring to, in real conditions, whether it was possible under such conditions for projectiles to fall inside the Old Town. And we have clearly managed to show that even without the influence of meteorological conditions, shells may indeed fall inside the Old Town on the assumption that certain ranges were used while firing. So please, there is no way I can testify about something that I did not study and something that I have never been tasked to study.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I reviewed the impacts inside the Old Town, perhaps that would have been a very different story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, this has gone on long enough. If you would listen to the question, if you are unable to answer it, say that. If you can answer it shortly or even as short as yes or no, please do so. But you spend a lot of time answering something that has nothing to do with the question in the end probably to justify why it is you can't answer the question. You don't need to justify that. For the moment, just say, "I can't answer it," if that is the position and we will get along much faster. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last few questions, sir: Since your report dealt with alleged targets outside the Old Town, if mortar shells were intentionally fired by the JNA into the Old Town at targets or what they perceived to be targets, you would have to modify your conclusions and change your report. Isn't that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the number of shells, had that been targeted deliberately, the number of shells would increase. First, of course, we would have to do all the calculations. But yes, the number of shells would increase. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you would have to change your conclusion if objects within the Old Town were targeted, that at certain times during the day on December 6th it actually was a primary target. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I would change any of my conclusions. Please, if you look at the portion where we have shown that the shell falls along its normal trajectory when a target outside the Old Town is targeted, we had the exact number of shells that were fired from a certain firing position against a certain target, then we could ascertain, had that particular target not been targeted, it would have been this much or that much, the number that we have given. And if we have information on a specific other target, then the number would increase by so much. But there is no reason for me to change my conclusion of the expert opinion now because the expert opinion only talks about targets outside the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, there is nothing in the damage that you saw in the Old Town that indicates that it could not have been the result of deliberate shelling. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my objection on the same grounds as yesterday when discussing damage. I do not wish to repeat myself. I do not wish to waste time, but I would like this witness not to be asked questions about damage because he's not competent to answer any such questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is nothing in the damage that you observed in the Old Town indicates that it could not have been caused by deliberate shelling. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the damage was caused by a mortar projectile explosions. Whether it was deliberate or not was something that I could not establish. I had no data based on which I could establish that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your report on page 99, you state "it cannot be concluded that fire from JNA mortars or other artillery and naval pieces was primarily directed towards Dubrovnik Old Town as its primary target." And you cite Nojko Marinovic and Zeljko Soldo. Since both of those individuals indicated the targeting was deliberate against the Old Town, and there are two JNA witnesses who indicated that there was mortar shelling that was fired upon the Old Town at alleged targets, based on that information, can you not conclude that fire was directed at the Old Town for some periods during the day of December 6th, 1991, and for some period of time it was a primary target?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, on page 89, on page 89 of the expert analysis in the conclusion on the -- on mortar fire, we concluded that based on everything that we showed, 27 120-millimetre shells and 106 82-millimetre shells could have landed inside the Old Town. It was based on those figures that we made the following conclusion: Grade I and II damage was considered, and we concluded following this analysis that a large number of shells would have fallen inside the Old Town. If you count the impacts inside the Old Town and compare them to our analysis, namely, that that was the result of shooting at targets outside the Old Town how could that conclusion possibly be that this was deliberate? The only logical conclusion was that certain weather conditions were in place, and there were positions that were putting the Old Town at risk. And that's why so many shells landed inside the Old Town. You can't call that deliberate. If you analyse targets that were outside the Old Town, this is what it clearly shows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you to assume these things, just listen to my question, please. Assume the testimony of two JNA witnesses, witnesses from the JNA, that there was shelling, mortar shelling in the Old Town because they thought that there was an objective, there was a mortar in the Old Town, and there was deliberate shelling into that Old Town. And also assume those two statements that you cited, those of Soldo and Marinovic where they both indicate shelling in the Old Town was deliberate. If you assume those two points, can you not agree that for a period of time, fire was directed by the JNA towards the Old Town as its primary target?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is something that I don't know about. There is no evidence. I have a statement by one of the two witnesses, Nojko Marinovic, the statement you showed me yesterday --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you what you have. I'm asking you to assume those facts. Two witnesses have testified here of intention shelling into the Old Town. A third witness for the Prosecution who also served in the JNA has testified of intentional shelling into the Old Town. That's Witness B. You assume the validity of those three statements, sir, as well as the validity of the two statements that you relied upon, the statements of Soldo and Marinovic. And if you assume those, do you agree, based on assuming those, that fire was directed towards the Old Town as its primary target? Can you not agree based on assuming those facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, sir, my understanding is that it's up to the Honourable Trial Chamber to judge whether those statements were truthful or not. It isn't my place to use their statements to make conclusions. I'm an expert. I have been called upon to study specific data. But not witness statements or witness testimonies, and this is nothing that I should base my opinion on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you as an expert, sir, what's known as a hypothetical question. If you assume the validity of those three statements, that the Old Town was deliberately targeted, as well as those two statements that you rely upon in your report, do you not agree that for a period of time on the 6th of December, fire was directed towards the Old Town as its primary target, if you assume the validity of those five statements?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is not a question for me. I'm an expert. I have put together an expert analysis. I'm not here to analyse witness statements or testimonies. As for Zeljko Soldo and Nojko Marinovic and their testimonies, all we took from them were the locations on the number of weapons, but that's all we had used their statements for, nor do I believe I'm entitled as an engineer to use anything else from their testimonies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, I am going to interrupt in place of Mr. Petrovic. I thought you were going on to put something else, but at the moment all you're putting to the witness is "if you assume" certain evidence, don't you accept the truth of their evidence? That's the effect of what you're putting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, I'm asking if he assumes certain evidence, does he not agree that the Old Town was targeted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But that's what I've just put to you in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But he has taken the view, Your Honour, that the Old Town was not targeted and it was as a result of collateral damage in his conclusions and varying the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I know that. That's very clear. What I'm pointing out is the question as you've now framed it really is not one that can be usefully dealt with by this witness. I thought you were directing your question at another aspect of that. But as you keep repeating it and reformulating it, it's becoming clear that that's really all you're asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll modify it and finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you assume, sir, that if you include the testimony of three witnesses that the Old Town was deliberately attacked on the 7th of December [sic], must you not modify your conclusions? And it's your conclusion that the Old Town was not deliberately attacked.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the kind of expert opinion that we made, I don't think the conclusion would be changed. We would need to include targets inside the Old Town. We would need all the information, what sort of weapons we used, how many projectiles were fired, and where they impacted. And then we could say, "Such and such a number of projectiles would fall that were targeting positions outside the Old Town" and it would have been normal to expect when these weapons are fired, since so many shells were fired, that out of a total number of shells that were fired a certain number fell inside the Old Town. But for you to expect me now to confirm something that I do not indeed know, nor have I heard any testimonies that the Old Town had been targeted deliberately, there are statements that I read, but specifically in terms of the percentage given by Nojko Marinovic, I think it was caused by frustration, and the same applies to Zeljko Soldo when he said that the attack on Srdj failed first, and it was only after the attack had filed that they had begun to target the Old Town. But this is of no relevance for my analysis because this is not the kind of analysis that I was involved in. My analysis analyses targets outside the Old Town. It was based on those targets that I reached my conclusion, namely that there was no deliberate shooting because a lot of projectiles fell there. It's all conditional. I should perhaps speak in terms a projectile would have fallen somewhere if we had, for example, a hundred projectiles falling on a certain firing position. In order for this expert opinion to be of any use to the Trial Chamber when studying all the testimonies, and then you said the witness then spoke about this fire position, so in that case they will go back to the expert analysis and say, okay, but we had five times the number of shells falling on that particular position, and that's what we need to look at. So that was the reason why we make this expert analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, your expert analysis does not include or was not based on the evidence of the two Defence witnesses who indicate that the Old Town was deliberately targeted or Witness B from the JNA who indicated that the Old Town was deliberately targeted. Isn't that correct? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you will remember that during my testimony before this Honourable Trial Chamber I said that the expert analysis ends with Ivan Negodic's testimony and that I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is - yes or no - did you include in your analysis those three witnesses? Just yes or no, sir.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in relation to the weapons' location and the number of weapons, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not include the testimonies of those three witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't include their entire testimonies. Only some of the facts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Petrovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vilicic, please, tell us specifically why you used these witness testimonies that you refer to in your report, for what sort of information?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For two kinds of information only. Firstly, the locations of the firing positions of the Croatian forces and the JNA, Nojko Marinovic in relation to the Croatian forces --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, no details. Why did you use those statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The word was testimonies first. It should be statements of individuals because they weren't witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Entirely technically correct, Mr. Weiner, but I think anybody will understand the transcript. Mr. Petrovic, you're having the same difficulty as Mr. Weiner. Press on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Indeed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, why, in order to obtain what sort of information exactly, did you use the witness statements that you referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only information we used was the location of the weapons and the number of weapons. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you analyse anything else based on those statements in addition to these groups of information that you just referred to?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing else. Because there was nothing else that we needed in order to approach this problem from a technical point of view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any other source of information that you used as to where the potential positions of the targets were or the potential locations of the firing positions?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next source of information was the map that the OTP submitted to us that was used, I believe, during Ivan Negodic's testimony. I think it was shown where you can see the C-4 firing position at 200 metres to the west of the Old Town in the direction of Ploce. 200 metres to the east of the Old Town, correction. This is something that is not included in Nojko Marinovic's statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, don't go any further into that. Just try to answer my question. Was that the only source of information that you used, the statements on the one hand and the maps on the other, that you used while defining the positions and the targets?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you had an opportunity to read the expert opinion of Jozo Poje, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While reading that opinion, I suppose you saw what method he used to determine the positions, which targets did he analyse?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He analysed hypothetical targets that were not there to begin with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, just tell me which ones. Which targets?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he analysed Ploce, Bogosica Park, but in relation to firing positions that were not there at all, for example a 120-millimetre mortar from Bosanka. It was only in annex 2 that he analysed the target of Ploce as targeted from Uskoplje by the 120-millimetre mortar. Speaking from memory, but I would have to look at it again in order to be more accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Jozo Poje? Did he do the same thing in his analysis that you did in yours? He assumed some positions, he assumed the targets, and he calculated the zone of dispersion, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. We never in cross-examination discussed Mr. Poje. It's outside the scope of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I please answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. Carry on, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can the witness please be shown P184, which is Jozo Poje's report. Since I'm not sure if the witness can locate it at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Together with the annexes, annex 1 and annex 2. So we need annex P184/1, /2, and /5, or at least that's what I believe. Your Honour, will you please instruct me now, shall we be going on until 11.00 or -- Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would it be more convenient to have the break for you then to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I was about to propose, Your Honour. I would like the witness to have some time to go through the document, and then we can proceed after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will realise that I am allowing you to enter into this simply to indicate in general terms whether the approach of the other expert was the same approach as this expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was precisely my intention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Beyond that, Mr. Weiner's objection would become valid.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully understand and agree with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now and resume at quarter past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, could you first please look at the document P184/2. That is an addendum to the expert analysis prepared by Jozo Poje, and please look at B/C/S page 0356729. Have you found this page?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the upper right-hand corner, you should see these numbers, the last three digits are 729.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find that page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Usher has the document in her hands.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find the number 729. I can only see 279.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only find 932. That's annex 2 the Jozo Poje expert report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may give you my copy so you can better find your way around. Could you please put it on the ELMO so that everyone can see the document. Let us just look at the upper part of the page and the beginning of the page, in fact. Just a little bit downwards. Thank you. Mr. Vilicic, could you please just read and focus on my question. Mr. Vilicic, the first sentence, can you please read it for us, the first sentence on this page.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Based on the recent information about the position of the Croatian army weapon positions around the Old Town of Dubrovnik, the dispersion patterns have been calculated."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, in this report that you have in front of you, is there any other source indicated other than this sentence that you have just read which is at the top of this page?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any other source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Further downwards in the same document, it reads: "Zarkovica firing position," then it says PA gun, that is anti-aircraft gun, north of the town. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, "firing position Zarkovica, PA gun, the beginning of the cable car, north of the Old Town."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, can you now turn to the second page of this document and please read what it says about mortar firing position and the target.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Anti-aircraft gun east of Ploce at 200 metres."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's ERN number --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ERN number 03340722F2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you look at point 184.5 referring to Uskoplje, please. Could you please read the first sentence only at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the map, the deployment of the 2nd Operational Group's forces on 2nd December 1991, see position of the battalion firing group of the 3rd Motorised Brigade in the Uskoplje sector if it was fired from the position at the anti-aircraft gun north of the town."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, we did not get the whole sentence. It was removed from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We don't need this document any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, you have seen how Jozo Poje has indicated potential firing positions and potential targets.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only in terms of the manner of marking potential targets and potential firing positions, in those terms, did you take an identical approach?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was my conditional target C-5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vilicic, could you also please tell me, based on what kind of analysis did you arrive at the conclusion that the Old Town had not been the target on the 6th of December? What kind of analysis?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on a ballistic analysis done on the basis of calculations, and we concluded that based on the figures and patterns of dispersion under normal conditions we concluded that a number of projectiles fell into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time attempt in your analysis to portray the sequence and dynamics of events of the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. This is a kind of static analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time entertain an ambition to explain how it all started and what everybody's intentions were?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not the subject of my analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, why did you at all in one segment of your analysis raise the issue of damage? What was your motivation for that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We analysed the damage only from the viewpoint of whether the roughly estimated degree of first- and second-rate damage corresponded to the number of shells falling in the Old Town while targeting the objectives outside the Old Town. So we detected a great similarity in the number of shells and the number that we have arrived in our calculations with respect to the damage incurred on buildings of grades I and II because those were the only ones that could have been deemed as directly hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move now to another subject. In principle and theoretically speaking, what is the ultimate range of a mortar?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the range achieved when firing at 45-degree angle on condition that other requirements for the table are fulfilled, which means that that was a standard plus-15 degree temperature, that the pressure was 760 millibars, that there was no wind, and provided that the target and the weapon were in the same plane. In other words, ideal conditions taken from the tables. Only under such conditions can this be achieved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does the term ultimate range mean?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means the maximum distance that a projectile can reach. It cannot reach beyond that distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the difference -- Mr. Vilicic, what is the difference between the ultimate range and the effective range of a weapon, successful range of a weapon? What is the difference between these two notions?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference because only individual shells reach an ultimate target. I said none of them can go beyond that. An effective range for mortars is two-thirds of the maximum range. That is what we call an effective range. Beyond that, the dispersion increases. And the accuracy also decreases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the ultimate range is a theoretical notion?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a maximum range in theory and under ideal conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood properly the answer to your previous question, an effective range of a mortar is two-thirds of the ultimate range?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Document P132. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, can you see on this map, or maybe it's -- the details are too small. Can you see the position of the Libertas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see. This is this darkened area. That's the hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you discern topographic characteristics of the terrain of the Hotel Libertas?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's at the elevation and after our yesterday's discussion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, can you see the topographic characteristics of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This map shows that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the altitude is 30 metres. That is what I wrote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, with respect to north, can you tell me at which slope is Libertas Hotel towards any point north of the Hotel Libertas?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the rear slope. Because you see that the contours increase as the altitude increases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, concerning -- can you see the battalion firing group -3 on this map? Can you please point it with a pointer.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is this B-3 firing group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see on this map an observation point of the commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade? Is it marked on this map?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 3rd Company, the 2nd Company. I think this would be the observation post. Yes, here it is. The observation point was close to Mocije or Mocije cave. So this would be the command post. And I suppose an observation post is there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour. He's saying "I suppose." He's just assuming. He's speculating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's valid. The marking is of the command post, I think, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where was the command post of the commander?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that I had just shown. It's named Mocinska Spilja, or Mocije cave, rather, that is the closest location to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, is it possible from the location of Mocije cave to guide or correct fire of the firing group of the 3rd Battalion of the 5th Brigade at the rear slope near the Libertas Hotel that you had previously indicated?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not possible. As you can see, behind the Libertas Hotel towards the observation post, the contours become more dense which means that the elevation there -- the altitude there was higher than that of the Libertas Hotel, and this hill here creates a cover. No, you can't see it because the Libertas Hotel altitude is not more than 20 metres, I believe, and that is an altitude that cannot be seen from this higher altitude as I can read from the contours. That would be over 100, even maybe 190 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next question: Could you please take the map that you had with you yesterday and that you used for calculations, and can you please also take a ruler. First, we need both maps. Please keep them there. Mr. Vilicic, first of all, on the map that Mrs. Usher is holding in her hands -- could you please take your ruler... First of all, on the map that is on the ELMO, use your ruler to measure the distance of the mark of the battalion group 3. Can you measure it in millimetres, how big it is.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the diameter?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the diameter of the position of the firing group 3.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4 millimetres. Just give me some more time. 3 and a half millimetres. I apologise. 4 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now, assuming that the scale of this map is 1 to 71.000, and that's something that we have no reason to doubt, tell me how much is 4 millimetres on a map with 1 to 71.000 scale?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said that 12 millimetres is 1.000 metres; therefore, 4 millimetres would be 333 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your map, can you please precisely indicate the position of the battalion firing group, the centre of this mark, please.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I can't see it on my map as on this one. Let me see. This centre is point 6. 5 millimetres. Just one moment. I need to calculate it. I apologise. 500 metres. Yes. It's 500 metres to the right of the point 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, can you find on your map the location where the battalion firing group was indicated -- as indicated in P132.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's a huge difference in the scale. But recalculating it, I may determine the location. So as I said, 500 metres would be here. Now, let me see what is the distance there. The average is 402. 150 metres. Just a moment, please. Well, approximately here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark this.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, on your map.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be approximately -- 500 is here. That's here. So this is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you answered my learned colleague's question, determined that the distance between this point and Libertas, did you mark it precisely as you did now?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I didn't have exact coordinates of the map. I now realise that I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, from the point that you have marked on your map, can you please put the map on the ELMO so that everyone can see it. So from that point, could you please calculate the distance to the Libertas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 6.000, 1200. So I'll take the centre point of Libertas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, it's all right. Take the centre.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's 6.250 plus... So that would be -- six and one-third. That would be 6.360 [as interpreted] metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vilicic. Can a 120-millimetre mortar hit an invisible target at the rear slope from the distance of 6.330 metres?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's impossible. That would be an ultimate range, and it would be out of control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could any effects be achieved on the target by firing at the distance of 6.330 metres in the ultimate range and at a rear slope? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's very difficult. It would be random shooting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, let's move to the next question. Just briefly, the Jugo wind, you said that while -- when Jugo blows, that is characterised by low air pressure.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the sky's overcast, the pressure is low. And that indicates the forthcoming rain. That's what ordinary folk would say, the drop of pressure which makes people feel bad, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for Bura, you said that it goes with high air pressure.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is generally clear, visibility at sea is great as opposed to the visibility which is reduced when Jugo blows. So you see crystal clear, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the tapes that you viewed, did you notice what was the weather like on the 6th of December? Was it cloudy?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see that it was clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just two or three more subjects, if we can cover very briefly. Yesterday, when you spoke about recoilless gun, you said that an armoured target can be hit at the distance of up to 1300 metres. Could this gun be used to shoot targets beyond that distance?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I made a slip of the tongue because I know that a new sight can indicate up to 2.000 metres because as I said the dispersion -- vertical dispersion pattern is two times two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that targets beyond 1300 metres can be shot at?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but with very low degree of precision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we would like to move on to the damage in front of St. Blaise church. If you can find it, P71, that is the film made by Djelo Jusic, 19th minute, 17 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the shortened version or his entire recording so that we Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond reach this time? Shall I play the entire original, 27.32 and stop at this timing, 19.17?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, I would kindly ask you to find the 19th minute and the 17th second.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said 19 minutes, 17 seconds?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll play it from 19.14. It's the Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please wait for my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, once again, in which direction relative to the Stradun do the slabs stretch, the slabs that cover the area around St. Blaise's church?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Relative to the canal you see on the Stradun, these slabs are rectangular. The sinkhole in the middle. So the slabs are rectangular at a right angle to the centre of the Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean at a degree of 90 degrees? At 90 degrees?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And you can see that on the film if you allow me to play it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, now --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- please play the film P145, the 58th second. That is the JNA film.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, what did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 58th second.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is second 55, and then it goes on, damage to the column, to the pillar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Freeze here. Please look. In which direction do the slabs stretch, the slabs covering the square in front of the church?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see they go from the church to the north of the church. Let's put it that way because the church is on the south side, and this is north-south. And now I'm showing west-east, and the material is thrown to the west. The slabs are thrown to the east. Yesterday I said that the projectile fell at an angle from the western direction, penetrated here, exploded. The debris was created and made this spherical trace. You see this depression here. The impact wave that was moving outside threw out these slabs, and this material coming from the hole was thrown backwards to the side where the angle of the projectile was smaller relative to the ground. That was the basic conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us clarify one more thing: These slabs covering the square in front of St. Blaise church are at a 90-degree angle relative to the Stradun?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need this film any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the little arrow he pointed north and south and west and east was all the same, with the little arrow on the computer when he had the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... I don't know what to make of that, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The little arrow that you use with the mouse when he was pointing north and south, and then he pointed east and west, and it was all the same, in front and behind of the crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, allow the witness to repeat it if this is unclear. I don't think this is unclear. But let us show it again. Let us show the directions again if my learned friend believes there is any confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, please, show us the film P145.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second 55.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, second 55. Freeze here. Now, slowly and carefully.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, I'll rewind it a bit. This is 46, second 50. Here, here we can see how the slabs go. They are parallel -- they are at a 90-degree angle to Stradun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, slowly and carefully show us where the west is.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, I'm showing the arrow points west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let the record show that the arrow on minute 58 -- or rather, second 58 on P145, the arrow points towards the top of the screen. Please show us east.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is east. East is in this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, for the record, let us note that the witness is pointing with the arrow towards the lower edge of the screen. Mr. Vilicic, please show us in which direction is the north.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let the record show that the witness is pointing towards the right edge of the screen. Where is south?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in this direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let the record show that the witness is pointing towards the left side of the screen as south.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, we will not be needing this any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Petrovic. It would help me if we could see that, now is as convenient as any time, from about 10 seconds before to about 10 after just to get that particular picture in perspective.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, now, kindly play this from second 48.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the bottom right corner, you see the time. At this moment is 07, 08. Those are seconds. I will move the picture. Look at the left number, which is now changing as I'm moving. Here is second 43.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Freeze for a moment. Now.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here you can see how --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vilicic, I'm just asking you kindly, in fact, the Trial Chamber is asking you to play the tape --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second 46 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't need comments. Just play it from second 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
